html:
Warning — do not read this file first. These are the reference answers for the three capstone engagements in Phase 16: Real-World Use Cases. Attempted your register, swimlanes, requirement list, fit-gap, and adoption plan? Then diff your logic here and redo the gaps — portfolio strength comes from the redo.

How to use: overlap check, then close the file. Read a milestone reference only after you have your own version; every milestone names the deliverable to hand a build team and the repo artifact (object, flow, service, report, permission set) where it becomes buildable; reasoning beside each table is the transferable skill; finish with the Grading Rubric and redo anything below reviewer-ready.

Use Case 1 — New CRM Rollout Discovery (BrightLogistics) Solutions

Milestone M1 — Stakeholder Register and RACI

Deliverable: 01_UC1_stakeholder_register.md + Stakeholder__c records.

#StakeholderRole in the rolloutPowerInterestQuadrantRACIEngagement strategy
1Greg NweshiCEO / executive sponsor, signs budget54High/HighAManage closely: weekly 15-min KPI check-in
2Operations DirectorOwns dispatch outcomes, headcount impact43High/med-lowAKeep satisfied: milestones and decisions only
3Driving Team LeadRepresents truckers who must ack loads35Med/HighRKeep informed: every workshop, first UAT cohort
4Billing ManagerInvoicing downstream of dispatch42High/lowCKeep satisfied: consult at scope changes only
5Dispatcher SMELives in the inbox; knows the real as-is25Low/HighRKeep informed: discovery partner, daily co-design
6Sales LeadQualifies inbound web inquiries34Med/HighRKeep informed: owns lead-source/cycle requirements
7Salesforce Admin / ITConfigures and owns the org34Med/HighRKeep informed: build liaison, permissions, deploys
8Change/Training LeadOwns go-live comms and retraining23Low/medCMonitor: escalates at go-live, owns UC3 later

Scores come from evidence: Greg can cancel the project; the Billing Manager sees outcomes second-hand.

RACI — four real activities, exactly one Accountable per row:

ActivitySponsorPMBusiness OwnerSMEIT/Admin
Prioritize backlogAIRCC
Write & approve requirementsCARRC
Build routing flowIACRR
Execute UAT & sign-offIRACI

Two smells to catch: two Accountables in one row (escalation ping-pong) and an SME marked Informed on UAT (the dispatcher must test the to-be, not hear about it).

Artifact you hand to a developer: one Stakeholder__c record per row with Influence__c, Interest__c, Power_Score__c, Interest_Score__c, RACI__c, Engagement_Level__c, plus RSVP tracking via force-app/main/default/flows/Stakeholder_RSVP_Tracking.flow-meta.xml.

md
UC1 Milestone 1 - Register (excerpt)
Greg Sponsor      | power 5 | interest 4 | RACI: A | manage closely
Ops Director      | power 4 | interest 3 | RACI: A | keep satisfied
Driving Team Lead | power 3 | interest 5 | RACI: R | keep informed
Billing Manager   | power 4 | interest 2 | RACI: C | keep satisfied
Dispatcher SME    | power 2 | interest 5 | RACI: R | keep informed

Reasoning: the Ops Director (power 4, interest 3) is high power / mid-low interest, so keep satisfied at milestones. The Dispatcher SME is the inverse (power 2, interest 5): keep informed and co-design daily — the as-is pain lives in his inbox.

Milestone M2 — Three Discovery Workshops and As-Is/To-Be Swimlanes

Deliverable: 02_UC1_workshops_and_maps.md + Process_Map__c records.

#WorkshopParticipantsAgenda (sums to 90 min)Decision of the day
W1Lead intake as-isDispatcher SME, Sales Lead, Admin (scribe), BA (facilitator)0-10 goals/rules · 10-35 draw as-is · 35-55 mark pain · 55-75 count steps/cycle · 75-90 agree pain listApprove pain list + cycle-time baseline
W2Dispatch handoff as-isDriving Team Lead, Ops Director, Dispatcher SME0-10 goals · 10-40 draw handoffs · 40-60 waste hunt · 60-80 root-cause 48h · 80-90 define "done"Agree the 4-hour healthy-dispatch definition
W3To-be design + KPICore team + Greg (last 20 min)0-10 recap · 10-40 draft to-be · 40-60 automation menu · 60-75 KPIs · 75-90 sign-offSponsor signs KPI targets and to-be process

As-is swimlane (baseline ~48h):

md
Swimlane: UC1 Lead Intake (as-is)   trigger: web form submitted   end: freight dispatched

Website   : [shipper submits web form] -> [form emails shared inbox]  !!
Inbox     :                            [lead sits 12-48h]             !! WAIT
Dispatcher:                            [reads email] -> [re-types into Excel]  !! RE-KEY
Sales Lead:                                          [maybe calls]  !! NO OWNERSHIP
Dispatcher:                                          [calls carrier manually]
Ops       :                                  [dispatch notes in Excel]  !! NO SYSTEM OF RECORD
                             (12-48h wait + same-day call) = ~48h cycle

Pains to mark on the map: inbox wait, Excel re-key, no owner on the next step, history trapped in a spreadsheet.

To-be swimlane (target under 4h, no re-entry):

md
Swimlane: UC1 Lead Intake (to-be)   trigger: web form submitted   end: freight dispatched

Website   : [shipper submits web form]
Salesforce: [auto-create Lead + source + Received_At] -> [dedupe check]
          : [auto-assign to queue by rules] -> [notify assignee]      >=80% no re-entry
Dispatcher: [opens assigned lead] -> [qualify in 1 call]
          : [dispatch captured: carrier, rate, ETA] -> [driver notified]
Driver    : [acknowledge load on phone] -> [status back to dispatcher]
Ops       : [KPI dashboard: cycle time + auto-assign rate]            target cycle < 4h

Every remaining to-be step earns its place; the inbox and the Excel re-key are deleted, not moved.

Metrics before/after — the proof the to-be is better:

MetricAs-isTo-be
Steps (lead to dispatch)95
Actors43
Handoffs across lanes63
Re-keying events30
Cycle time (hours)48<4
Auto-assignment0%>=80%

Artifact you hand to a developer: two Process_Map__c records carrying the metrics as data:

apex
Process_Map__c asIs = new Process_Map__c(Name = 'UC1 Lead Intake As-Is',
  Step_Count__c = 9, Actor_Count__c = 4, Cycle_Time_Days__c = 2);
Process_Map__c toBe = new Process_Map__c(Name = 'UC1 Lead Intake To-Be',
  Step_Count__c = 5, Actor_Count__c = 3, Cycle_Time_Days__c = 0.2);

Reasoning: greenfield still needs as-is maps — the manual process is the pain that justifies the change, and the before/after metrics are what the sponsor buys. Routing uses assignment rules/queues plus a flow for the 4-hour escalation (declarative first, Apex only if the rules outgrow configuration).

Milestone M3 — BRD and Traceable Requirement List

Deliverable: 03_UC1_BRD.md + 14 Business_Requirement__c records, approved via the repo approval process.

BRD sections (7): background & goals · scope (in/out explicit) · stakeholders & RACI · as-is/to-be summary · functional requirements · non-functional + data + reporting · assumptions, dependencies, open questions. In scope: web capture, dedupe, auto-assignment, dispatch capture, driver ack, reporting. Out of scope: carrier TMS integration, rate-card engine, marketing automation.

IDRequirementTypeMoSCoWSourceAcceptance criterion

R-102Duplicates by email + company are flagged for merge review before dispatch workDataMustSales LeadSecond match flagged Duplicate_Flag__c

Traceability rule: every requirement links to at least one story (M4) and one UAT test case. Coverage = tested / total; a story with no test case is a coverage gap, not "nearly done."

Artifact you hand to a developer: Business_Requirement__c with Requirement_Type__c, Priority__c, Status__c, Value_Score__c, Acceptance_Criteria__c; sign-off runs the repo approval process + force-app/main/default/flows/Requirement_Approval_Routing.flow-meta.xml, publishing Requirement_Status_Changed__e. Approval turns "written" into "approved."

Reasoning: numbering lets developers and testers trace each requirement to code, tests, and UAT; MoSCoW is set against this release's KPI — R-114 is a Could because tuning follows measured load.

Deliverable: 05_UC1_data_dictionary.md — field-by-field, no open decisions.

Relationship decisions: dispatch is an Opportunity on the shipper Account (Lookup — an opportunity exists without a dispatch); driver ack is a related Task/Event. A custom dispatch object would be Master-Detail to Account only if it has no life without the shipper.

Analytic tooling you documented rather than re-invented (already in the repo): Stakeholder__c (Influence__c, Interest__c, Power_Score__c, RACI__c, Engagement_Level__c); Process_Map__c (Step_Count__c, Actor_Count__c, Cycle_Time_Days__c, As_Is_Description__c, To_Be_Description__c); Business_Requirement__c (Requirement_Type__c, Priority__c, Status__c, Value_Score__c, Acceptance_Criteria__c); User_Story__c (Story_Points__c, Priority__c, Priority_Score__c); UAT_Test_Case__c (Status__c, Severity__c, Signed_Off__c, story lookup).

Reasoning: design for reporting first — that is why Received_At__c/Dispatched_At__c are DateTimes (computable KPIs), not prose in a notes field.

Use Case 2 — Legacy System Migration Gap Analysis (BrightLogistics billing/files) Solutions

Milestone M1 — As-Is Process Maps for the Legacy Flows

Deliverable: 06_UC2_as-is_maps.md + Process_Map__c records + numbered legacy-rules inventory.

md
Swimlane: UC2 FreightBill invoicing (as-is)  trigger: dispatch done  end: invoice paid
Dispatcher : [marks job done in Excel]                            !!
Billing Clk: [opens FreightBill] -> [re-keys job]                 !! RE-KEY, single machine
System FB  : [calculates charge] -> [prints invoice PDF]
Billing Clk: [saves PDF to \\server\invoices\2024\random.pdf]     !! NO INDEX
Customer   : [pays] -> Clk [marks paid in Excel]                  !! SECOND SYSTEM OF RECORD
Rule FB-3  : manual line adjustments, no log                      !! UNAUDITED
Documents  : rate PDFs + PODs found only by the clerk (Rule FB-7)

Swimlane: UC2 Refund (as-is)  trigger: dispute  end: refund settled
Billing Clk: [dispute email] -> [pulls Excel row]
Supervisor : [verbal OK] or [paper form]       !! NO CHAIN, NO SLA
Billing Clk: [refunds in bank portal] -> [annotates Excel]  !! UNTRACEABLE

Reasoning — the classic migration trap: conflating "no fit" with "build custom." FG-03 (impact 20) triggers a decision record evaluating AppExchange packages — not code; most "gaps" are habits (FB-7's clerk-only retrieval).

Milestone M3 — Data Migration, Cleaning, and Quarantine Requirements

Data-quality checks (pass/fail each): DQ-1 Name non-empty (else quarantine) · DQ-2 Tax_Id__c unique (else quarantine + merge review) · DQ-3 zip/state consistent (else quarantine) · DQ-4 Balance__c variance = 0 (else block cutover) · DQ-5 open invoices carry an approved status (else block batch) · DQ-6 file names match the convention (else manual index queue).

Quarantine process: suspect rows land in staging (or status Quarantined with reason) — never in the live master. The Billing Manager triages daily: Restore (fix, approve to master) or Reject (stays out, counted in reconciliation, owner named). Exit: zero quarantined open-billing records at cutover.

Cutover plan:

StepEntry criteriaExit criteria
FreezeT-1 day, no new FreightBill entriesOps Director confirms freeze
ExtractFrozenRow counts + hash totals recorded
Clean/DedupeExtract verifiedDQ checks pass; duplicates merged
ValidateClean set existsReconciliation: counts and balances match source to the penny
LoadValidation signed by Billing ManagerLoad log: loaded / quarantined / rejected counts
Reconcile (T+1)Load completeSponsor + Billing Manager sign; defects logged in UAT_Test_Case__c

Artifact you hand to a developer: the mapping table is the load spec (external IDs, transforms, required flags); DQ checks become validation rules; quarantine status becomes a picklist + list view; reconciliation becomes a report requirement.

Reasoning: cutover is where silent assumptions live — the mapping table forces every legacy field to declare its fate (map, transform, de-scope) before the freeze.

Go/No-Go checklist (UC2)
- [ ] 100% Critical resolved
- [ ] 100% High resolved or formally deferred (owner named)

Use Case 3 — Post-Launch Change Management Solutions

Milestone M1 — Adoption Audit

Deliverable: 11_UC3_adoption_audit.md — per persona, per metric, baseline vs target, before any training spend.

PersonaMetricBaselineTargetByData source
DispatchersActive (logged in + record work)35%70%Day 60Login history + lead/dispatch counts
DispatchersAuto-assignment used (no re-entry)20%80%Day 60Auto_Assigned__c
DriversLoads acknowledged in app15%60%Day 60Dispatch_Status__c = Acked
Ops managersDashboard/report views weekly20%60%Day 60Report view logs
AdminsConfig ownership (in-platform changes)55%90%Day 60Setup audit trail
All personasFlow runs succeeding (six academy flows)40%85%Day 60Flow execution logs

Root causes the audit must conclude: drivers at 15% have an access + value problem (never trained, unclear WIIFM) → mobile ack training and driver-first messaging; managers at 20% see a dashboard that answers no real question → demo it against their decisions; dispatchers commit 20% re-entry out of habit → retrain and freeze the inbox alias; admins route changes 45% of the time through IT → hand over config ownership with a permission-set review. The blended 40% of target hides all four.

Artifact you hand to a developer: metric definitions become report requirements; adoption fields follow the ChangeManagementService pattern on Account (Adoption_Stage__c, UAT_Signoff_Date__c, Adoption_Day_Count__c).

Reasoning: diagnosis beats new features — the audit comes first because it decides whether to spend on training, UX, or messaging.

Cross-cutting checks (a deliverable fails review if any is unchecked):

  • Every requirement has a pass/fail acceptance check
  • End-to-end traceability: requirement -> story -> UAT case, no coverage gaps
  • Every gap and de-scope has a decision owner, options, and recorded trade-off
  • No gap went to custom build before configure/extend/package were evaluated
  • KPIs anchored: <4h and >=80% (UC1), zero silent data loss (UC2), per-persona trend (UC3)
  • Adoption reported per persona against baseline and target — never one blended number
  • Artifacts exist as prose + repo evidence (objects, flows, reports, permission set, tests)
  • A build team can implement without decisions you should have made

The common thread across all three use cases is decisions with trade-offs, documented — the same signature move in a register, a swimlane, a fit-gap row, and an adoption audit. Which artifact proves requirements are testable end-to-end? The requirement -> story -> test-case traceability chain. And when adoption drops to 40% three months after launch, the best first move is diagnosing usage per persona — then retrain, re-message, re-simplify — before building another feature.

If a milestone scored below reviewer-ready, redo just that artifact in your portfolio and re-score. That redo — not this file — is what you carry to the CBA exam and to a real engagement.
